articles.title: One TypeScript file lives in five repositories, and four of our five sites currently agree
articles.excerpt: CogniPrep is one of five products built by the same company. The others are a food scanner, a rental listing watcher, a pub quiz host and a creator outreach tool. Five domains, five repositories, five…
articles.body: CogniPrep is one of five products built by the same company. The others are a food scanner, a rental listing watcher, a pub quiz host and a creator outreach tool. Five domains, five repositories, five deploy pipelines, one company behind all of them. That last fact is the awkward one. A crawler looking at five sites that link to each other has no reason to believe they share a publisher rather than being five strangers swapping links. So each site emits the same company as structured data, and the fact that the node is byte-identical across all five is the entire claim. Which leads to the part I want to write about: if agreement between five independently deployed sites is the signal, then reading the file in one repository tells you almost nothing. You have to check from the outside.
articles.author: Daniel Pertu

articles.title: Scraping YouTube comments without the API quota (and the bug where 300 comments meant one thread)
articles.excerpt: The YouTube Data API gives you 10,000 quota units a day by default. Reading comments costs 1 unit per page of up to I built a comments scraper that reads what youtube.com shows a logged-out visitor in…
articles.body: The YouTube Data API gives you 10,000 quota units a day by default. Reading comments costs 1 unit per page of up to 100 comments, which sounds generous until you need replies too, or more than a handful of videos, or a second project running on the same key. People who analyse comments at any scale hit that wall pretty quickly. I built a comments scraper that reads what youtube.com shows a logged-out visitor instead, so there is no key and no quota. A few things I learned on the way, in case you are building something similar. "300 comments" should mean 300 comments My first version had one limit, maxComments , and replies counted toward it. Seemed reasonable. Then a test asked for 300 comments with replies on a popular music video and got back 1 comment and its 299 replies .

articles.body: When scraping YouTube videos, channels, or comments data, HTTP 403, 429, CAPTCHA, and empty responses are common obstacles. Many developers assume the code is at fault, but the core causes typically reside in outbound proxies, request frequencies, client fingerprints, and dynamic DOM rendering. In 2026, YouTube’s automated verification has grown significantly more complex. Selecting the right scraping stack and tuning your network environment is far more effective than endlessly debugging source code. This article analyzes tool selection, YouTube’s anti-scraping mechanics, and step-by-step error troubleshooting. I. How to Choose a YouTube Scraper?

articles.body: You’re testing a form a few screens into your Flutter app, with the fields already filled in. The spacing looks cramped, so you adjust it in the code and trigger a hot reload . The app picks up the change, and the form is still on screen with your values in it. That’s the loop Flutter developers rely on. articles.body: Every month, I used to repeat the same reporting routine: open Google Analytics 4 open Google Search Console change the date range export the data compare it with the previous month build charts write observations repeat everything for another website At some point, I realized that most of this process was not analysis. It was data collection and formatting. So I decided to automate it with Python. The goal was simple: Run one command and generate the same monthly website report I would normally build manually. This article explains the structure I used, what data I collect, and a few lessons I learned while building it. articles.excerpt: Localizing SaaS for the Philippine Wedding Market: What I Learned Quick Answer: Localizing a wedding planning tool for the Philippines isn’t just translating text. You have to match local wedding cust…
articles.body: Localizing SaaS for the Philippine Wedding Market: What I Learned Quick Answer: Localizing a wedding planning tool for the Philippines isn’t just translating text. You have to match local wedding customs, billing expectations (PHP, fees, and formatting), and payment behavior (especially GCash). In this post, I’ll share the design decisions and failure-proofing steps we learned the hard way. Introduction If you’re building SaaS for the Philippine wedding market, you probably already know the obvious parts: use the right language, set prices in the right currency, and don’t assume users have the same payment options as elsewhere. What surprised me was how quickly “small” localization gaps became conversion blockers.

articles.title: Below Review
articles.excerpt: Below is Netflix’s go at a “What if Jaws but…” type of story set in Newfoundland starring Josh Hartnett that starts off with a promising hook and closes with a hole-y, disappointing end.
articles.body: Below is now streaming on Netflix. Set in a tiny, remote coastal town that’s suddenly facing a mysterious threat from the sea, Netflix’s new drama/horror series Below is in the unfortunate position of being compared to Widow’s Bay, the other show that already did that this year. It’s a “what if Jaws but…” vehicle for Josh Hartnett, on a career upswing with things like Oppenheimer , Trap (yes, Trap), and a great episode of Black Mirror . And while he’s doing all he can here, in a thick Newfoundland accent no less, to carry the six-episode series, Below can’t keep pace with the other show. A relatively solid first half of episodes is done in by the back three that messily (and occasionally ridiculously) tie up a story that hasn’t fully found its sea legs.

articles.title: NASA’s SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Mission Overview
articles.excerpt: NASA and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than Tuesday, Oct. 13 to launch scientific investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station.
articles.body: NASA’s SpaceX 35th commercial resupply mission will launch on the company’s Dragon spacecraft on the SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket to deliver research and supplies to the International Space Station. NASA NASA and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than Tuesday, Oct. 13 to launch scientific investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station.  Loaded with more than 6,300 pounds of supplies, the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft will lift off aboard the company’s Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Following its arrival to the orbital complex, Dragon will autonomously dock to the space-facing port of the space station’s Harmony module.  NASA will stream launch and…

articles.excerpt: OpenAI is launching a new Intelligent UI feature in ChatGPT that allows the chatbot to answer your questions with interactive visuals. The update, which is rolling out to all users alongside GPT-6, gi…
articles.body: OpenAI is launching a new Intelligent UI feature in ChatGPT that allows the chatbot to answer your questions with interactive visuals. The update, which is rolling out to all users alongside GPT-6, gives ChatGPT the ability to combine a text response with diagrams, charts, forms, tappable buttons, and more. In a blog post explaining the change , OpenAI says it trained GPT-6 when to generate interactive visuals over text, as well as how to format them in its response.
